classification.difficultyReason: Convert the rotation to revolutions and the radius to metres, then calculate the total circular distance.

inlines.text: In a Physics experiment, students spin a mass around on the end of a thread.
The thread is 80 cm in length. The mass is 5 kg.
Calculate the distance the weight travels if it spins a total of
Give your answer in metres rounded to two decimal places.

spec.sourceRegion: Q12 figure below the prompt at left
spec.description: A black person silhouette holds a thread overhead. The thread extends down-right to a black mass marker on a dashed horizontal elliptical trajectory. Annotation arrows identify thread and Weight.
spec.mathematics: The thread is the radius of the circular trajectory; the ellipse represents that circle in perspective. No extra numerical diagram labels are introduced.
spec.answerVisibility: All figure elements are permanent student-visible givens.

answer.worked:
The thread is the radius of the circular path.
$$\begin{align*}
r &= \frac{80}{100}=0.8\text{ m}\\
\text{Revolutions} &= \frac{4230}{360}=11.75\\
\text{Distance} &= 11.75\times 2\pi r\\
\text{Distance} &= 11.75\times 2\pi\times 0.8\\
\text{Distance} &= 18.8\pi\text{ m}\\
\text{Distance} &\approx 59.06\text{ m}
\end{align*}$$
